objective: Smallest usable authenticated stone generation, appraisal and cutting loop with three grades, immutable generation-time outcome, exact custody and atomic fees/results/replay recovery.

recommendation.choice: New independent ItemState.stone_ref containing an opaque server-generated 128/256-bit serial and public grade/table digest, plus a private AccountStore.shared_stones registry containing immutable frozen outcome/appraisal evidence and irreversible cut tombstones. Use actual workshop NPC and a typed player route; generation, appraisal and cut each commit the affected account(s), registry CAS, wallet, exact carrier and receipt together.
recommendation.why: The serial remains unchanged across whole-item storage/trade, so result does not reroll when a physical UID is normalized or an owner changes. Existing shared trade serializes full ItemState. Keeping hidden outcome outside ItemState avoids existing nested JSON client snapshot leaks. A serial is additional logical identity, not a substitute or second authority for UserItem UID.
usableFirstSlice: Register three distinct non-stackable quantity-one rough-stone templates with explicit normal icon/item-info/i18n bindings.

Authenticate a real workshop NPC Buy/Appraise/Cut page in the current map/range and derive account/character/actor from the active session. Implement matching typed frontend actions and result receipts.

NPC Buy creates stone ItemState, random serial, frozen selected output and table digest plus the generation receipt in one durable transaction. Preview quotes never draw a result or allocate identities.

Appraise charges once and records a frozen coarse hint; Cut consumes exactly one owned original carrier and releases all frozen outputs only after an atomic successful transaction. An already-cut serial is a permanent tombstone.

Preserve serial through actual full ItemState storage and shared trade, validate global duplicate carrier identities, and use strict affected account revision + registry revision CAS for trade-versus-cut races.
Only bind tested existing real gem/material outputs. Building consumption is a later real consumer; normal ore and weapon-upgrade behavior stay intact.
notEnough: Pure recipe/rules module without NPC/client routes.
Generic FreshItemGrant publish alone: current mining publication is in-memory and cannot atomically create and persist a sealed stone.
A per-character outcome ledger alone for tradeable stones.

rootSpecificAnswers.newItemStatePrivateRecord: Full ItemState storage and shared trade can retain a serde-default private field, but a hidden seed/outcome in that field is not safely private with today's client snapshot implementation. Use a public opaque reference in ItemState and keep the frozen outcome/salt entirely in a server-only global record. If root chooses full private ItemState records, it must recursively redact all embedded JSON-string carriers and adapt every UserItem-only custody route first; this is larger than the reference+registry choice.
rootSpecificAnswers.pgAllocator: There is NO registered production PostgreSQL UserItemUidAllocator in the current code. UserItemUidAllocator exposes initialize_file/open_file, and trusted with_item_uid_allocator explicitly rejects any configured account_store_database_url. item_identity_reservation/item_identity_postgres/config_item_identity modules are cfg(test) unregistered candidates; their CAS reservation SQL is not a runtime binding and must not be claimed as production.
rootSpecificAnswers.globalRegistryHeroPattern: Tractable, but explicit. Copy the Hero domain's structural validator, fixed authorized record scope, no-deletion tombstones, source-version receipt validation, load/restore protection, mutation-plan projection and same-transaction PG CAS integration into separate stone domain files. Add new AccountStore fields/clone/normalization/schema gating and every relevant match/permit deliberately. AccountsWithGlobal only authorizes existing global shop stock; it is not a generic permission for new fields. A File-only first transaction can persist full AccountStore JSON but must still implement domain scope validation and block PG/Mirror activation until the registry's transaction projection is complete.
rootSpecificAnswers.publicActivation: The new serial separates immutable roll identity from physical UID but does not close the incomplete all-issuers authority/census boundary. Controlled File opt-in testing can exercise real authenticated routes, but public gateway activation remains blocked until a single deployed UID authority and every required issuer/custody/census backend are covered. Do not add a second independent high-water service.

immutableSealContract.generation: Preflight actual fee, exact full capacity and complete carrier shape before mint. Generate serial/private salt once on accepted generation, choose and store frozen complete outputs under one immutable table SHA, record minted carrier+registry+fee+receipt in the same durable account commit.
immutableSealContract.randomness: Do not derive hidden outcome from public UID or time. Frozen sampled outcome plus random private salt is sufficient for deterministic later reveal; if a public commitment is emitted, hash a canonically encoded serial+grade+table digest+private random salt+frozen output, not a low-entropy unsalted outcome that can be brute-forced.
immutableSealContract.noReroll: Changing owner, physical slot/UID, login, table/key rotation or repeating appraisal never reseeds. Preserve original table-specific decision and original receipt; a cut cannot be undone or tombstone evicted.
immutableSealContract.ownership: Accept only exact current authenticated durable bag carrier with the registry's serial/template/grade/version. Registry is not keyed to initial purchaser for ownership. Strict revisions serialize trade-versus-cut; reject foreign query or old owner without leaking private record existence.
immutableSealContract.duplication: Each live serial must have at most one authoritative custody location across complete declared held/personal/shared source domains. A Cut tombstone stops repeated output but alone does not stop duplicate tradable stones from defrauding another buyer; protect carrier uniqueness too.
immutableSealContract.appraisal: Emit only explicitly whitelisted coarse hint, public grade/cost and spent/available status to current owner. Never generic-serialize the registry, seed, selected output or private salt into UserItem/world snapshot/action error/log.
immutableSealContract.cut: Stage source removal, full fee and the entire frozen output batch; use existing actual capacity/weight/carrier checks and the same trusted UID service. No partial delivery or fee/source mutation on a known failure. UID prefix burned during a later failure remains retired rather than reused.
immutableSealContract.receipts: Idempotency identity includes durable actor+request+operation/serial/expected source version and quoted price/catalog digest. Exact replay returns original terminal receipt; conflicting reuse rejects. Query original receipt from confirmed durable source after reopen, not a live cache.
immutableSealContract.unknown: Known precommit failure leaves source/wallet/ledger unchanged. Unknown publication freezes source writes across reopen/restart; exact original receipt reconciliation only. PostCommit live projection failure must not mint/refund again.
immutableSealContract.bounds: Bound records, request grammar, output batch, checkpoint JSON and reserve space for future terminal receipts. No pruning unresolved operation records or cut tombstones without a separately safe durable archive.
immutableSealContract.custody: Stack size1/count1; reject split/merge/equip/refine or unsupported fresh rehydration for rough stones. Adapt full original custody returns, never substitute a new serial or fresh mint.

limitations: This note is architecture exploration, not a source/test result permit.
Some ordinary shared trade normalization can reassign physical UIDs on collision; serial preserves roll identity but does not authorize that custody behavior or close UID migration.
Existing mining output publication is not durable account atomic, and the shipped RubyOre name mismatch is separate existing behavior.
A server-only ItemState private result is not currently globally redacted at client boundaries.
No schema/security implementation or PG migrations were executed; root/frontier must independently review actual patch.
